To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current Australian pathways to higher educational context, with its focus on English language proficiency as the main determinant of success, is a major obstacle to intercultural understanding and that this obstacle may be addressed through the use of methodologies that acknowledge multiplicity.
intercultural learning is enhanced by the use of methodologies that acknowledge cultural differences and multiplicities, which in turn may serve to facilitate inclusive pedagogical practices.

the promotion of interculturalism is best served by: (1) a commitment to diversity; (2) a commitment to collaboration; (3) an acknowledgment of the presence of multiple identities; (4) an understanding of the importance of the role of the tutor in facilitating intercultural learning; and (5) the development of pedagogical methodologies that support these commitments.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a more inclusive pedagogy that will enable the development of interculturally competent pathways tutors and students, who are more able to engage with the challenges that arise when working in diverse contexts.
how the Australian higher education system can better respond to and accommodate diversity in the interests of promoting a more inclusive, equitable and interculturally aware learning environment.
the ways that cultural diversity can be fostered and supported within the context of pathways to higher education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the promotion of interculturalism in Australian pathways to Higher Education is a complex and challenging task, but one that is essential if we are to move beyond the limitations of monoculturalism.
intercultural education in the Australian context is not a reality.
the promotion of interculturalism in Australian pathways to university requires the development and implementation of a pedagogical methodology that is both inclusive and critical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
interculturality is a process of learning and unlearning.
the promotion of diversity in Australian pathways to Higher Education can be enhanced through the development of a more inclusive and collaborative pedagogical approach.
the more we are aware and acknowledge our own cultural biases and the more we are able to see and accept that other cultures are different, the more we will be able to develop interculturally.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a more inclusive pedagogy is needed to address diversity and interculturality in Australian pathways to university.
the development of inclusive pedagogies that promote interculturability is a necessary step toward the achievement of the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals.

the promotion of interculturality in pathway education requires an acknowledgement of the multiplicity of cultural perspectives and the recognition that these are not fixed but fluid and dynamic, as well as a commitment to the promotion of collaborative and inclusive practices.
